analysis:
This batch contains only documentation: a new changelog.d entry (changelog.d/glm-tensor-parallel-stop-race.md, head lines 1-4) and edits to docs/architecture/inference.md. The inference.md edits are the Last-updated date (line 3), the GLM tensor-parallel paragraph (~line 4040), and the committed-token-channel paragraph (~line 4048). No executable code is in the supplied units.

The documented behavior is a latent stop-race fix in GLM tensor parallel's one-token decode (`GLM5NextTensorParallelStepLoop`, `ClusterGLMTensorParallel.speculativeDepth` 0). A rank that stopped commits nothing more but still ends at a stop token its peer commits. Rank 0's count and finish then cross in one small agreement, and rank 1 adopts them unless it stopped on its own (`QwenTensorParallelStopRule.reconcile`). This is an availability/liveness improvement for T-010 (DoS via stalled collectives). The doc says no released pair is affected, since all v0.10.6 pairs load the NextN layer and use MTP rounds.

The docs also drop the older wording that sampled decode runs one token per step, and now state that greedy and sampled requests decode in MTP rounds. This matches the later sentence "Sampled requests decode in rounds too", so it is a consistency fix.

No trust-boundary, encryption, attestation, authorization, or data-exposure claims change. The sealed all-sum, the AES-GCM link, and the prefix-cache partitioning text (T-041) are carried over unchanged.

Open question for code-level review: the actual implementation (the step loop and `QwenTensorParallelStopRule.reconcile`) is not supplied. This pass cannot verify that rank 1 adopting rank 0's count and finish cannot be abused by a malicious peer. The pair link is keyed and sealed, so a peer is presumably a trusted cluster member, but that is outside the evidence supplied. The documentation claims are not verified against source.
